tasks.name: Motion slice: move a state node and commit the layout (baseline numeric X/Y fields versus drag with optimistic position)

current.note: open the node select; ids from index.html; geometry not measured, default P applies

current.why: MEASURED server-side p50 of POST layout, n=20, loopback, 2026-09-29; browser render time not measured
current.note: baseline task() locks the whole page and drops further clicks while the request runs

proposed.note: point at the node on the canvas; geometry belongs to the canvas lane
pointer down: MB-01 acknowledgement within 100 ms limit, 50 ms target
move to the drop position; frames follow MB-09, no waiting
pointer up: position shown immediately with the pending marker (optimistic class O1)

proposed.why: PREDICTION budget: kernel ack shown; the user can continue while it is pending, so 100 ms is a conservative upper bound
proposed.note: commit budget target is 300 ms (MB-03); measured server p95 was 26 ms

assumptions: PREDICTION only. KLM constants K 0.20 s, P 1.1 s, B 0.10 s per press or release, H 0.40 s, M 1.35 s (Card, Moran and Newell 1980 as tabulated at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystroke-level_model, opened 2026-09-29); band plus or minus 21 percent (same source). Expert, error-free, routine execution only.

Click convention: B is 0.10 s per button press or release (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystroke-level_model, opened 2026-09-29), so a click is two B ops (press, release) and is written as two B ops. The T04 proposed drag is likewise P B (press) P B (release).

Task id is suffixed -motion because T02, T04, T06 and T08 are used for different flows in other lanes' files; ids are unique across files this way. The base task (persona, frequency) is the shared task of the same number.

This file is the motion and performance slice. The interaction shape (drag versus numeric fields) is decided by the interaction and canvas lanes; this aspect contributes only the R operations and the rule that no operation blocks input. The drag is decomposed as P B P B (point, press, move, release) rather than the D operator.
The current flow has no keyboard-only path; the non-dragging path required by WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 belongs to the interaction lane.
R in the current flow is server-side only (Python http.client against uvicorn on loopback, n=20, this PC shared with other agents). A browser probe in a hidden tab was discarded as confounded.

Predicted sums under the two-B convention (PREDICTION, band plus or minus 21 percent): current 10.668 s (8.43 to 12.91); proposed 3.850 s (3.04 to 4.66); gap 6.82 s. R basis is asymmetric on purpose: current uses the MEASURED server p50 of 0.018 s, proposed uses the 0.100 s budget. That is conservative against the proposal; with R = 0.018 s for both, proposed is 3.768 s and the gap 6.90 s. Computed by .tmp/latency/klm.py.

assumptions: PREDICTION only; same constants and band as T04. The predicted times are equal by construction: the decision changes what the user sees during the wait, not the wait.

Click convention: B is 0.10 s per button press or release (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystroke-level_model, opened 2026-09-29), so a click is two B ops (press, release) and is written as two B ops. The T04 proposed drag is likewise P B (press) P B (release).

Reading the outcome is not modelled (KLM does not cover reading).
Live provider and other long jobs (model check, mutation, TLC) are not measured by this lane; their durations are UNKNOWN.
Predicted sums (two-B convention): 4.746 s (3.75 to 5.74) in both flows; the 2.096 s wait is 44 percent of it. R is the MEASURED server p50 in both flows.

tasks.name: Motion slice: open the four chapters of a change review

current.note: baseline has no chapters; a details summary toggles instantly, R 0 (press)

proposed.note: expansion uses motion.transition.continuity (240 ms) and is interruptible, so the next input is processed at once (MB-19); waiting share w = 0 by design (press)

assumptions: PREDICTION only. Both flows are equal in KLM terms because animations are interruptible and no R operation is charged. Sensitivity, computed in docs/adr/0066-hci-motion-performance.md: if each of the four expansions blocked input for its full duration (waiting share w = 1), a 240 ms tween adds 0.96 s and a 400 ms tween adds 1.60 s to the 6.55 s baseline; the point estimate at 400 ms (8.15 s) is 0.22 s above the baseline band's upper edge (7.93 s) but the bands overlap (6.44 to 9.86 s versus 5.17 to 7.93 s), so no time claim is made either way.

Click convention: B is 0.10 s per button press or release (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystroke-level_model, opened 2026-09-29), so a click is two B ops (press, release) and is written as two B ops. The T04 proposed drag is likewise P B (press) P B (release).

Task id is suffixed -motion because T02, T04, T06 and T08 are used for different flows in other lanes' files; ids are unique across files this way. The base task (persona, frequency) is the shared task of the same number.
The chapter structure is the review lane's design; this slice only carries the animation waiting cost.
Predicted sums (two-B convention): 6.55 s (5.17 to 7.93) in both flows without blocking; with blocking tweens (w = 1) 7.51 s at 240 ms and 8.15 s at 400 ms.
